title: Delegate non-performance removal is automatic and purely quantitative, requiring no one's judgment
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.5.2 sets two thresholds and makes breach self-executing: "A Delegate is **automatically** offboarded if they fail to vote on ≥ 3 proposals in a row; or maintain a voting percentage less than 85%."

The two conditions catch different failure shapes. Three in a row catches abandonment — a delegate who has gone dark, lost their key, or lost interest, detected fast. The 85% floor catches chronic partial neglect, which the consecutive-miss test would never trip if the delegate votes just often enough to reset the counter.

Automaticity is the load-bearing property. Every other removal channel in the framework runs through a body with discretion: the Spark Risk Council can offboard immediately for misconduct (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.5.3), and disqualification grounds trigger an SRC-initiated removal vote (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.2.5). Participation, by contrast, is measured and applied without anyone deciding — which matters precisely because the actor who would otherwise decide, the Spark Foundation, appointed and pays the delegate.

The corresponding weakness is that mechanical thresholds measure only presence. A delegate who votes on 100% of proposals without reading them satisfies both conditions perfectly, and only the discretionary channels can address that.
description: Three consecutive missed votes or a participation rate below 85% offboards a Delegate by rule, so enforcement cannot be softened by the same body that appointed them.
